<!--[[File:PSimon 2019.jpg|alt=Patrice Simon, Professor at University Paul Sabatier, Toulouse (France)|thumb|Patrice Simon, Professor at University Paul Sabatier, Toulouse (France)]]-->

'''Patrice Simon''' (born 1969) is a French chemist in the field of [[materials science]] and [[electrochemistry]]. He is currently a Distinguished Professor at the [[Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier University|Université de Toulouse]] (former Université Toulouse III Paul Sabatier) since 2007.

His research focuses on the synthesis and characterization of materials for electrochemical [[energy storage]] applications, particularly for power systems ([[supercapacitor]]s and [[Battery pack|batteries]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://patrice-simon.fr/index.php/en/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=patrice-simon.fr}}</ref> More specifically, he develops advanced electrochemical characterization techniques to understand the charge storage mechanisms in confined environments, a research topic he initiated in 2006 with [[Yury Gogotsi]].

He currently serves as Director of the research network on electrochemical energy storage [https://www.energie-rs2e.com/en RS2E].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our team |url=https://www.energie-rs2e.com/en/our-team |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=RS2E |language=en}}</ref> Alongside Hélène Burlet (CEA), he also leads the "Priority Research Programs and Equipment" [https://www.pepr-batteries.fr/en/the-pepr/ (PEPR) Batteries], funded as part of the national battery acceleration strategy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Batteries |url=https://anr.fr/fr/france-2030/programmes-et-equipements-prioritaires-de-recherche-pepr/batteries/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=Agence nationale de la recherche |language=fr}}</ref>

Patrice Simon is Fellow of the [https://www.academie-sciences.fr/en/patrice-simon French Academy of Sciences],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Patrice Simon {{!}} Académie des sciences |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/en/node/2443 |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=www.academie-sciences.fr}}</ref> of the [[French Academy of Technologies]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Simon Patrice |url=https://www.academie-technologies.fr/academiciens/simon-patrice/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=Académie des technologies |language=fr}}</ref> He was also appointed as Fellow of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts|European Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-13 |title=Members - European Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/simonchimie-ups-tlse-fr/member/ |access-date=2025-04-09 |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Simon Patrice |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Simon_Patrice |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

==Biography==
Simon studied at [[École Nationale Supérieure des Ingénieurs en Arts Chimiques et Technologiques]] (ENSIACET) in [[Toulouse]], graduating with M.S. in metallurgy (1992) and Ph.D. in Materials science (1996). Thereafter he worked as assistant professor of Electrochemistry at the [[Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers]] in [[Paris]], and from 2001 at the [https://cirimat.fr/ CIRIMAT] laboratory of materials science, [[Université Paul Sabatier]], Toulouse. He received his D.Sc. from [[Université Paul Sabatier]] in 2002 and was appointed full Professor of Materials Sciences at [https://cirimat.fr/ CIRIMAT] in 2007. He was promoted as Distinguished Professor in 2014. From 2010 to 2017 he served as Director of the European Research Institute [https://alistore.eu/presentation ALISTORE ERI].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Presentation |url=https://alistore.eu/presentation |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=alistore.eu}}</ref> He was awarded two ERC Grants, in 2012 and 2020.

== Research contributions ==
[[Supercapacitor]]s are energy storage devices that have similar form factors to [[Battery pack|batteries]], but offer higher power and a longer [[Charge cycle|cycle life]]. A type of supercapacitors, called [[Double-layer capacitance|Electrochemical Double Layer Capacitors (EDLCs)]], use high surface area [[porous carbon]] as active materials. In these devices, charge storage is achieved electrostatically under polarization at the electrolyte / carbon interface, by reversible adsorption of ions from an electrolyte onto the carbon surface. Together with Prof [[Yury Gogotsi]] ([[Drexel University Sacramento|Drexel university, USA]]), he demonstrated that ions from an electrolyte could partially desolvate to access small size nanopores (thought to be un-accessible) in porous carbon electrodes ([[Science (journal)|Science]] 2006<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chmiola |first=J. |last2=Yushin |first2=G. |last3=Gogotsi |first3=Y. |last4=Portet |first4=C. |last5=Simon |first5=P. |last6=Taberna |first6=P. L. |date=2006-09-22 |title=Anomalous Increase in Carbon Capacitance at Pore Sizes Less Than 1 Nanometer |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1132195 |journal=Science |volume=313 |issue=5794 |pages=1760–1763 |doi=10.1126/science.1132195}}</ref>). His research may results in advances in commercial products. Modelling approaches were developed in collaboration with theoreticians to describe ion dynamics and organization in confined pores.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Futamura |first=Ryusuke |last2=Iiyama |first2=Taku |last3=Takasaki |first3=Yuma |last4=Gogotsi |first4=Yury |last5=Biggs |first5=Mark J. |last6=Salanne |first6=Mathieu |last7=Ségalini |first7=Julie |last8=Simon |first8=Patrice |last9=Kaneko |first9=Katsumi |date=December 2017 |title=Partial breaking of the Coulombic ordering of ionic liquids confined in carbon nanopores |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat4974 |journal=Nature Materials |language=en |volume=16 |issue=12 |pages=1225–1232 |doi=10.1038/nmat4974 |issn=1476-4660|pmc=5702543 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Merlet |first=C. |last2=Péan |first2=C. |last3=Rotenberg |first3=B. |last4=Madden |first4=P.
